title: Magnetic fields and field patterns; Magnetic materials, domains and permeability; Fields of currents (quantitative); Force on moving charges
qualification: AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MG01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MG01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; MG01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MG01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MG01-1#N.3, MG03-1#N.3a, MG04-1#N.3, NEW-magnetic-materials-1#N.2, MG01-1#N.5, MG03-1#N.6b, MG04-1#N.5, NEW-magnetic-materials-1#N.4, MG01-1#N.7, MG03-1#N.12b, MG04-1#N.9, NEW-magnetic-materials-1#N.5.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Solenoid
items.clue: Long coil whose inside pattern is straight, parallel and evenly spaced.

items.label: Compass needle
items.clue: Pointer whose north end shows which way the pattern runs at that place.

items.label: Magnetic field
items.clue: Region produced by moving charges that pushes on currents and on iron or steel.

items.label: Field lines
items.clue: Closed loops, never crossing, drawn closer together where the effect is stronger.

questions.stem: Point C is at the centre of a bar magnet, inside it. Point D is just outside the magnet, beside its centre. How does the magnitude of the magnetic field at C compare with that at D?

options.text: Greater at D, as field lines end at the poles and none is inside
Zero at both points, since the middle of a magnet is not magnetic
The same at both, as the magnet's field has one strength everywhere
Greater at C, as the closed field lines are crowded inside the magnet

questions.stem: An electron moves toward the right side of the page through a uniform magnetic field directed out of the page. What is the direction of the magnetic force exerted on the electron at this instant?

options.text: Toward the top of the page
Toward the bottom of the page
Out of the page, along B
Left, opposite its motion

questions.stem: A long straight wire of diameter 0.010 m carries a current of 12 A. Point P is 0.045 m from the surface of the wire. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field produced by the wire at P? (Use μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.)
Which of the following produces a magnetic field? Ignore Earth's field and Earth's motion.

options.text: A charged plastic ring held at rest on a stand
A charged plastic ring spinning about its central axis
An uncharged copper ring spinning about its central axis
An unmagnetized iron ring, held at rest on a stand

questions.stem: A long, straight, vertical wire carries a steady current upwards. Point P is 5.0 cm due east of the wire, level with it. What is the direction of the magnetic field of the wire at P?

options.text: Due south, at a tangent to a circle around the wire
Due east, directly away from the wire along a radius
Due north, at a tangent to a circle centred on the wire
Vertically upwards, parallel to the direction of the current

questions.explanation: Right thumb up, along the current: the fingers curl around the wire, and on its east side they point due north. The field is a tangent to a circle centred on the wire.

questions.stem: A proton moves in a circular path of radius r in a uniform magnetic field, with its velocity perpendicular to the field. A second proton moves in the same field with twice the speed, its velocity also perpendicular to the field. Only magnetic forces are exerted on the protons. The radius of the second proton's circular path is kr. What is k?

options.text: ½

questions.stem: Two long straight parallel wires, 1 and 2, are a distance d apart. Wire 1 carries a current I, and wire 2 carries a current 3I in the same direction. Point P is on the line joining the wires, between them, at the location where the net magnetic field produced by the two wires is zero. Ignore Earth's magnetic field. Which expression gives the distance from wire 1 to P?

A particle with charge q moves at constant speed v around a circle of radius r. The circulating charge acts as a small current loop, which is a magnetic dipole. Which expression gives the average current associated with the particle's motion?

options.text: qv/r
q
qv/(2πr)
2πrq/v

questions.stem: You look at the left end of a long solenoid. Seen from there, the current in its turns flows clockwise. Which end of the solenoid is its north end?

options.text: The left end, the one you are looking at
The right end, the far end from you
Neither: inside, the field is uniform, so there are no poles
It depends on the size of the current in the turns

questions.explanation: Fingers clockwise as seen from the left, so the thumb points to the right. Inside, the field runs left to right and leaves through the right end. Field lines leave a north end, so that end is N.

questions.stem: A proton moves at 2.0 × 10⁴ m/s toward the right side of the page through a region that contains a uniform electric field of magnitude 3.0 × 10³ N/C directed toward the bottom of the page and a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.050 T directed into the page. The gravitational force on the proton is negligible. What is the magnitude of the net force exerted on the proton at this instant? (Use e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.)

A long solenoid with N turns and length L has a field of magnitude B₀ inside it when the current is I. A second long solenoid has the same number of turns N spread over a length 2L and twice the radius, and it carries the same current I. What is the magnitude of the field inside the second solenoid?

An iron nail does not attract a steel paper clip. After the nail has been stroked several times in one direction with one pole of a strong magnet, it does attract the paper clip. Which explanation of these observations is correct?

options.text: It contained no magnetic dipoles until the stroking created them
The stroking moved some of the magnet's magnetism into the nail
The stroking charged its ends oppositely, as rubbing charges a balloon
Its domains pointed in random directions until stroking aligned them
